tasks.title: First dictionary
tasks.statement: You are given the price list {«яблоко»: 50, «банан»: 70}. Add «киви» for 90, raise the price of «яблоко» to 55, delete «банан», and print the whole dictionary. You should get `{'яблоко': 55, 'киви': 90}`.

tasks.title: Price of a product
tasks.statement: Write a function price_of(prices, name): the price of the product name from the dictionary prices, or 0 if there is no such product. The program must not crash on an unknown product.
tasks.hint: prices.get(name, 0) -- the second argument is the default value.

tasks.title: Dictionary with a new pair
tasks.statement: Write a function with_item(d, key, value): a new dictionary, a copy of d with the pair key: value added (or replaced). The original dictionary d must not be changed.
tasks.hint: Copy the dictionary, then assign result[key] = value and return result.

tasks.title: Word frequencies
tasks.statement: Write a function count_words(words): a dictionary "word -> how many times it occurred in the list". Use the pattern counts.get(word, 0) + 1.
tasks.hint: for w in words: counts[w] = counts.get(w, 0) + 1.

tasks.title: Cart total
tasks.statement: Write a function total_price(prices, cart): prices holds the product prices, cart is a dictionary "product -> number of items". Return the total cost. Products that are not in the price list cost nothing.
tasks.hint: total += prices.get(name, 0) * qty for each pair in cart.items().

tasks.title: Word -> length
tasks.statement: Write a function length_map(words): a dictionary where the key is a word from the list and the value is its length.
tasks.hint: result[word] = len(word) on each turn of the loop.

tasks.title: Is there such a value
tasks.statement: Write a function has_value(d, value): True if value occurs among the VALUES of the dictionary d (not among the keys), otherwise False.
tasks.hint: The word in on the dictionary itself looks at keys; the values come from d.values().

tasks.title: The most expensive
tasks.statement: Write a function most_expensive(prices): the name of the most expensive product in a non-empty price list. Loop over the pairs with prices.items() and remember the best one.
tasks.hint: If best_price is None or price > best_price, update both variables.
